chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one who narrated it, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, the mu'min is so noble before Allah that if he were to ask Him for Jannah and whatever is in it, He would give him that without anything diminishing from His dominion. And indeed, the kafir is so insignificant before Allah that if he were to ask Him for the world and whatever is in it, He would give him that without anything diminishing from His dominion. And indeed, Allah surely watches over His believing servant through affliction just as an absent one looks after his family with gifts, and He surely protects him from the world just as a physician protects the sick person.

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the worldly life and its temporary possessions
key_terms.الطَّبِيبُ: the physician, used as an analogy for protective restraint
key_terms.الْجَنَّةَ: Jannah, the eternal abode that Allah can grant without any loss to His dominion
key_terms.الْكَافِرَ: the disbeliever, whose receipt of worldly things does not indicate honor before Allah
key_terms.الْمَرِيضَ: the sick person who is prevented from what may harm him
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنَ: the believing servant whose rank before Allah is honored
key_terms.بِالْبَلَاءِ: through affliction or trial, as a mode of divine tending and care
key_terms.مُلْكِهِ: His dominion, which is not diminished by giving

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah afflict the believer while protecting him from the world?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the immense worth of the mu'min before Allah and the insignificance of worldly possession in relation to His absolute dominion. It also explains that afflictions upon the believer are a form of divine care, and that being withheld from worldly attachment can itself be a mercy and protection.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from the one who reported it, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Momin is prestigious to Allahazwj to the extent that if he was to ask Himazwj for the Paradise and whatever is in it, Heazwj would Give him that from without there being a reduction from Hisazwj Kingdom by anything; and that disbeliever is so abased to Allahazwj to the extent that if he were to ask Himazwj for the world with whatever is in it, Heazwj would Give him that from without there being a reduction from Hisazwj Kingdom by anything; and Allahazwj has Pledged Hisazwj Momin servant with the affliction just as the absentee tends to undertake the sending of souvenirs to his family, but Heazwj Shields him from the world just as the physician shields the patient’.
en.sarwar: 28. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from his narrators, from al-Halabi from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“A believer is so important to Allah that if he asks Him paradise and all that is therein. He will give it to him without any shortages caused to His kingdom. The unbeliever is so insignificant before Allah that if he asks the whole world and all that is therein. He will give it to him without any shortages caused in His kingdom. Allah is committed to sending misfortune to the believers just like one’s commitment to his family in sending them souvenirs during his absence from home. He holds him back from worldly things like the physician who holds back a patient from certain food items.”
